authority: T0 C0-B symmetry no-go certificate; not a TECT claim, causal-emergence theorem, or cosmology
statement: For a finite substrate state, an automorphism-invariant strict order cannot compare two events in the same automorphism orbit; hence a deterministic natural equivariant selector is empty when the automorphism group is vertex-transitive. The stronger 2-transitive ordered-pair proof remains valid without finiteness. Under fixed labels or a declared pullback identification, an exactly reversal-invariant state likewise cannot uniquely select a nonempty arrow when covariance sends the order to its opposite. The theorem leaves smaller-orbit relational states, stochastic or non-single-valued sector selection, and infinite transitive models open; it fixes a conditional C0-B gate rather than deriving causality or rejecting C0-B.

general_theorem.substrate: finite event set X with state s
general_theorem.symmetry: Aut(s) acts on X; the empty-order corollary assumes vertex transitivity
general_theorem.selector: deterministic, natural under relabeling, and valued in strict partial orders
general_theorem.orbitwise_conclusion: no two points in one finite automorphism orbit are comparable
general_theorem.transitive_conclusion: if Aut(s) is vertex-transitive, the selected relation C(s) is empty
general_theorem.proof: if x<C(gx), invariance and transitivity iterate around the finite order of g to give x<Cx
general_theorem.two_transitive_corollary: one selected ordered pair forces its reverse, so a 2-transitive invariant strict order is empty even without finite X
general_theorem.infinite_boundary: translations act transitively on Z while the usual order is nonempty and invariant, so the finite transitive theorem is not extended to infinite X
general_theorem.reversal_corollary: under fixed labels or a declared pullback identification, if Rs=s and covariance gives C(Rs)=C(s)^op, then a deterministic strict selected relation is empty
